The Story of King Shubh

I bow to Lord Jinendra, who brings welfare to the world, and I write the story of King Shubh.

King Shubh of Mithila Nagar and Queen Manorama had a son named Devrati. Devrati was virtuous and wise. No fault or vice ever touched him.

One day, the clairvoyant monk Devguru came to Mithila with his monastic group. King Shubh, along with many worthy souls, went to worship the monks. After serving and worshipping the monastic group, he heard the discourse on dharma. At the end, he asked the monk about his future: "Yogiraj, please tell me — where will my next birth be?" The monk replied, "O King, listen — through the ripening of sinful karma, in your next life you will be born as a large worm in your own excrement. When you enter the city, filth will enter your mouth, your royal umbrella will break, and on the seventh day from today, you will die from a lightning strike." Truly, through the ripening of sin, all things happen. The monk spoke these words to the king with great fearlessness. And it is right that yogis have no fear of any kind.

The monk's prediction about Shubh began to come true. One day, as he was returning home and entering the house, his horse's hoof kicked up some filth that fell into his mouth. And as he moved a little further, a strong wind broke his royal umbrella. Truly, through the ripening of sinful karma, nothing is impossible.

He then called his son Devrati and said, "Son, through the ripening of my sinful karma, after death I will become a five-coloured worm in my own excrement. At that time, you must kill me, so that I may attain a better birth." Although Shubh was now fairly certain that the monk's words would come true, some doubt remained in his mind. Out of fear of lightning, he had a large, strong iron chest brought and ordered his servants to place it in the deep waters of the Ganga, so that he could sit inside it. He thought, "Lightning does not affect water. Through this means, I may be saved." But this was foolishness, for the words of omniscient beings never prove false.

On the seventh day, lightning struck the iron chest in the water, and King Shubh died. Through the ripening of his karma, he was reborn as a five-coloured worm in his own excrement. His son Devrati, remembering his father's instruction, found the worm and killed it, so that Shubh could attain a better birth. Through this act of compassion, Shubh was reborn as a human again. He remembered his past lives, took initiation as a monk, and through dedicated spiritual practice, ultimately attained liberation.

This story teaches that the words of omniscient beings never prove false. King Shubh tried to escape his predicted fate by hiding in an iron chest in the river, but lightning struck him anyway. The wise should understand that karma is inexorable, and one cannot escape the fruits of one's actions. The only refuge is in the practice of dharma and the pursuit of liberation.
